carrier_gaps_found.statement: SKILL.md:180 declares BestPrice's vendor-measured magnitudes 'not client-quotable' and requires them 'resolved against a current primary source *before any client-facing claim*'. greek-shopping-surfaces.md:13-17 then supplies both magnitudes (~6.9M and ~40.8M visits/month) AND a ratio derived from exactly them - 'on the same vendor's numbers Skroutz's traffic is roughly 6× larger' (grader-checked: 40.8/6.9 = 5.91) - and closes with a prohibition on only one direction of the comparison: 'Do not tell a client BestPrice out-trafficks Skroutz.'
carrier_gaps_found.the_ruling_asked_for: DOES THE DERIVED RATIO INHERIT THE PROHIBITION? YES. Three grounds. (i) Epistemic: a ratio of two unaudited vendor estimates is not more reliable than either, and the error compounds rather than cancels; the stated ground of the prohibition therefore applies with at least equal force to the ratio. (ii) Identity: the ratio IS the two magnitudes with the units cancelled - it is the same claim, not a different one, and a rule that bans the figures while releasing their quotient bans nothing. (iii) The file's own asymmetry proves the point: it forbids the comparative claim in the direction a client might want and hands over the opposite comparative claim as usable fact, which reads as permission to tell a client that Skroutz out-traffics BestPrice by about six times. That is precisely the reading SKILL.md:180 says 'was being read here as permission to cite with a caveat'.
carrier_gaps_found.scope_of_the_ruling: greek-shopping-surfaces.md is an OPERATOR surface, so carrying the figures and the ratio in that file is legitimate under the reader test and nothing needs deleting. What is missing is the client-facing status of the derived ratio, which the file leaves undefined and SKILL.md:180 does not name. The fix is one clause on :17 extending 'not client-quotable' to anything computed from those figures.
carrier_gaps_found.did_it_bite_this_run: No, and that is not evidence the carrier works. e2.md:57 refused all magnitudes and quoted no ratio: 'τα κρατάει εκτός πελατειακού κειμένου μέχρι να επαληθευτούν σε πρωτογενή πηγή'. e5_specific_adjudication_overproduction_.the_question: e5 is 3,058 words for a prompt whose honest answer is 'I cannot, here is what I need'. The executor flagged this as its own most uncertain call.
e5_specific_adjudication_overproduction_.verdict: THE RIGHT DELIVERABLE IN KIND, OVERPRODUCED IN DEGREE - and the overproduction is concentrated in two identifiable places rather than spread through it.
e5_specific_adjudication_overproduction_.why_the_kind_is_right: e5.4 explicitly licenses it: 'offering the analysis framework or a capture checklist while waiting is acceptable and does not fail.' More than that, the prompt asks four questions and a bare refusal answers none of them. The capture brief in S3 is not padding - it is the deliverable's actual product, and it is better than a screenshot request because it names the fields that decide whether the capture is worth taking (the Absent/Present distinction on every row, full cited URLs rather than domains, the ad copy, logged-out state). S2 is the strongest section in the file and could not be shorter: it establishes that 'the SERP' for a local-intent query is not one object, which changes what the client is asking for, and it needs no data to say. That is genuine information gain from a session with zero inputs.
e5_specific_adjudication_overproduction_.where_it_overproduces: (i) S4, the difficulty section, is 17 lines explaining the arithmetic of an instrument that cannot be run at all, and it is where the run's most consequential error lives (D1). A three-line statement - no score, here are the five inputs, the capture supplies the first - would have carried the same content with less surface to be wrong on. (ii) S6's four seven-field actions are heavier than the situation: A1 (choose the locations) and A2 (take the capture) are load-bearing, while A3 (a second capture) and A4 (decide about a subscription) are decisions about an analysis that does not exist yet and would sit better as two lines inside A2's expected impact. The seven-field contract is a good rule that does not scale down to a two-step unblock.
e5_specific_adjudication_overproduction_.the_test_applied: Would a client reading this be better served by a shorter version? For S1-S3 and S5, no - each earns its length by changing what the client does next. For S4 and S6, yes. Roughly 800 of the 3,058 words are ceremony, and the section carrying most of it is the section that got its arithmetic wrong. That correlation is the argument: length in a zero-data deliverable is surface area for error, because there is nothing to check the writing against.
